title: Daemon threads — features, use cases, advantages, disadvantages

s1_definition.profdef: A **daemon thread** is a background service thread that does NOT prevent the JVM from exiting. When ALL non-daemon (user) threads finish, the JVM terminates — killing all daemon threads abruptly without running `finally` blocks or shutdown hooks on those threads. Set via `thread.setDaemon(true)` BEFORE `start()`. Use cases: garbage collector (GC), background cache refresh, heartbeat monitoring, log flushing. The main thread and threads created by user threads are non-daemon by default. Daemon threads inherit the daemon status of their parent thread. A thread CANNOT change its daemon status after `start()` — throws `IllegalThreadStateException`.
s1_definition.analogy: **Non-daemon (user) threads** = bank tellers serving customers. The bank stays OPEN as long as at least ONE teller is serving. **Daemon threads** = the cleaning crew working in the background. They sweep floors, empty bins, refresh water coolers. When the LAST teller finishes and goes home (last user thread ends), the bank CLOSES immediately — cleaning crew is kicked out mid-sweep, no chance to finish! They don't get to complete their work or clean up. Use daemons for background tasks that are OPTIONAL — the bank can close without them finishing.
s1_definition.oneliner: Daemon = background, JVM exits when all user threads finish (kills daemons). User = foreground, JVM waits for them. setDaemon(true) BEFORE start(). GC is a daemon. Main thread is non-daemon.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** A **daemon thread** is a background service thread that does NOT prevent the JVM from exiting. When ALL non-daemon (user) threads finish, the JVM terminates — killing all daemon threads abruptly without running `finally` blocks or shutdown hooks on those threads. Set via `thread.setDaemon(true)` BEFORE `start()`. Use cases: garbage collector (GC), background cache refresh, heartbeat monitoring, log flushing. The main thread and threads created by user threads are non-daemon by default. Daemon threads inherit the daemon status of their parent thread. A thread CANNOT change its daemon status after `start()` — throws `IllegalThreadStateException`.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** **Non-daemon (user) threads** = bank tellers serving customers. The bank stays OPEN as long as at least ONE teller is serving. **Daemon threads** = the cleaning crew working in the background. They sweep floors, empty bins, refresh water coolers. When the LAST teller finishes and goes home (last user thread ends), the bank CLOSES immediately — cleaning crew is kicked out mid-sweep, no chance to finish! They don't get to complete their work or clean up. Use daemons for background tasks that are OPTIONAL — the bank can close without them finishing.

**One line to remember:** Daemon = background, JVM exits when all user threads finish (kills daemons). User = foreground, JVM waits for them. setDaemon(true) BEFORE start(). GC is a daemon. Main thread is non-daemon.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The bank needed background tasks that shouldn't block JVM shutdown:** (1) Cache warming: refresh account balances every 30 seconds. (2) Heartbeat: ping health-check endpoint every 10 seconds. (3) Log flusher: batch-write audit logs every 5 seconds. All three are OPTIONAL — if the main trading service shuts down, these should NOT keep the JVM alive. Fix: all three as daemon threads. When the trading service (user thread) finishes → JVM exits → daemon threads killed. But: log flusher had a `finally { flushRemaining() }` that was skipped on JVM exit → last 5 seconds of logs lost. Fix: moved critical flush to a shutdown hook (runs before JVM exit).

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** JVM starts → main thread (non-daemon) begins executing.

**Step 2.** Main thread creates 3 daemon threads: cache refresher, heartbeat, log flusher. All `setDaemon(true)` before `start()`.

**Step 3.** Main thread starts trading service (non-daemon worker threads). 200 user threads process trades.

**Step 4.** Trading service finishes → 200 user threads terminate → main thread returns from `main()`.

**Step 5.** JVM checks: any non-daemon threads alive? NO → JVM exits → 3 daemon threads killed immediately. Cache refresh mid-operation → killed. Heartbeat mid-ping → killed. Log flusher's finally block → SKIPPED!
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ JVM EXIT BEHAVIOR ═══

  NON-DAEMON (user) threads:           DAEMON threads:
  ├─ Main thread                        ├─ GC thread
  ├─ Trading worker-1                   ├─ Cache refresher
  ├─ Trading worker-200                 ├─ Heartbeat
  └─ JVM WAITS for ALL to finish       └─ JVM KILLS on exit!

  Timeline:
  t=0:   main starts, daemons start
  t=10:  200 workers start (non-daemon)
  t=60:  all 200 workers finish
  t=60:  main returns → JVM checks → no user threads → EXIT!
  t=60:  daemons KILLED mid-execution! No cleanup!

  ═══ WHEN TO USE ═══
  Daemon: cache refresh, heartbeat, monitoring, GC, log rotation
  User:   trade processing, payment settlement, data migration
  Rule:   if task MUST complete → NON-daemon!
          if task is optional background → daemon!
```
sections.s5c_hld:
```
  ═══ HLD — Daemon vs User Threads in Trading Service ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Trading Service (JVM)                            │
  │                                                    │
  │  USER threads (JVM waits):                        │
  │  ├─ main                                           │
  │  ├─ trade-worker-1..200 (ThreadPool, non-daemon)  │
  │  └─ settlement-worker-1..50                       │
  │                                                    │
  │  DAEMON threads (JVM kills on exit):              │
  │  ├─ cache-refresher (every 30s)                   │
  │  ├─ heartbeat-monitor (every 10s)                 │
  │  ├─ log-flusher (every 5s)                        │
  │  └─ GC threads (JVM internal)                     │
  │                                                    │
  │  Shutdown: workers finish → JVM exits → daemons die│
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — Thread Daemon Flag ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Thread                               │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────── │
  │  - daemon: boolean (default: false)  │
  │  - name: String                       │
  │  - priority: int                      │
  │  - group: ThreadGroup                │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────── │
  │  + setDaemon(boolean): void          │  MUST be before start()!
  │  + isDaemon(): boolean               │
  │  + start(): void                     │
  │                                        │
  │  Rules:                               │
  │  1. setDaemon after start → ISE!     │
  │  2. Child inherits parent's daemon   │
  │  3. Main thread: non-daemon          │
  │  4. JVM exits when: 0 non-daemon    │
  │     threads alive                     │
  │  5. finally in daemon: NOT guaranteed│
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  ThreadFactory for daemon pool:
  r -> { Thread t = new Thread(r);
         t.setDaemon(true);
         t.setName("bg-worker");
         return t; }
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A daemon thread is a background service thread that does NOT prevent JVM exit. When all non-daemon (user) threads terminate, the JVM exits immediately — killing all daemon threads without running their finally blocks. Set via `setDaemon(true)` BEFORE `start()`. Child threads inherit the daemon status of their parent. Main thread is non-daemon. The GC is a daemon thread.

Use daemon for: cache refresh, heartbeat monitoring, log rotation, background cleanup — tasks where abrupt termination is acceptable. Use non-daemon for: trade processing, payment settlement, data migration — tasks that MUST complete. Critical pitfall: `finally` blocks in daemon threads may NOT execute on JVM exit — don't rely on them for critical cleanup. Use shutdown hooks (`Runtime.addShutdownHook()`) instead. In banking: cache refresher and heartbeat as daemons — they stop automatically when the trading service shuts down. Log flusher: initially daemon, but lost last 5 seconds of logs on shutdown. Moved critical flush to shutdown hook.

keyPoints: Background threads: JVM exits when only daemons remain
